title: Industrial Asset Event Standard (IAES) 2.1 — Specification Release
description:
A MINOR release of the Industrial Asset Event Standard. Nothing it adds changes the bytes or the meaning of an event a 2.0 producer emits.

A specification release is one indivisible object: the specification, the governance document, the schemas and the RFC record, published under one tag. manifest.json is published with the GitHub release for this tag and carries a SHA-256 of each normative file, taken from that tag, so anyone can verify what they were served.

What 2.1 adds

  • A new event type, asset.state (IAES-RFC-010): whether an asset is up or down, planned or unplanned, why, and what it was doing while up — the facts MTBF, MTTR and availability are computed from, as ISO 14224:2016 asks them to be collected. Its schema is a new file at a new URI, https://iaes.dev/schema/v2/asset.state; the eight 2.0 schemas are unchanged, byte for byte.
  • content_hash by RFC 8785 (JCS) (IAES-RFC-011) for events that declare 2.1 or a later 2.x minor. An event that declares 2.0 keeps the 2.0 computation, so a retried 2.0 event keeps its hash.
  • Where an RFC lives (IAES-RFC-013): a Draft stays in its pull request until it reaches Review.

The version history in IAES_SPEC.md states the release, its known risks and its migration.
